'''Deborah Frank Lockhart''' is a mathematician known for her work with the [[National Science Foundation]].

==Career==
Lockhart graduated in 1965 from the [[Bronx High School of Science]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://alumni.bxscience.edu/?page=notablealumni|title=Notable Alumni-Bronx High School of Science Alumni Association|accessdate=Feb 10, 2015}}</ref> She received her BS in mathematics from [[New York University]],<ref name=LinkedIn>{{cite web|url=https://www.linkedin.com/profile/view?id=152544664|title=Deborah Lockhart|location=LinkedIn|accessdate=Feb 10, 2015}}</ref> and went on to receive her Ph.D. from [[Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute]] in the area of [[continuum mechanics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.awm-math.org/newsletter/199711/workshop/|title=Report on the 1997 Association for Women in Mathematics Conference in Stanford (from AWM Nesletter)|accessdate=Feb 10, 2015|archive-date=September 23, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923181007/http://www.awm-math.org/newsletter/199711/workshop/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Lockhart went on to work at [[SUNY Geneseo]] before moving to [[Michigan Technological University]] in 1976.<ref name=LinkedIn /> She began working as a program director at the [[National Science Foundation]] in 1988, later becoming a deputy division director and acting division director before, in 2016, being named deputy assistant director of the Directorate for Mathematical and Physical Sciences.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/mps/mps_webpage_documents/appointments/dr._deborah_lockhart.pdf|title=Appointment of Dr. Deborah Lockhart as Deputy Assistant Director, Directorate for Mathematical and Physical Sciences, National Science Foundation|first=F. Fleming|last=Crim|date=March 8, 2016|publisher=National Science Foundation}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==

In 2012, Lockhart became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref name="ams">{{cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|publisher=ams.org|accessdate=Feb 10, 2015|archive-date=August 25, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|url-status=dead}}</ref> Also that year, she became a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.aaas.org/news/aaas-members-elected-fellows-2 | title=AAAS Members Elected as Fellows | work=AAAS Website | date=30 November 2012 | accessdate=Feb 10, 2015}}</ref> She is also the 2021 recipient of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM) Prize for Distinguished Service to the Profession.<ref>{{Cite web|title=AN21 Prize Spotlight|url=https://sinews.siam.org/Details-Page/an21-prize-spotlight|access-date=2021-07-18|website=SIAM News|language=en-US}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
*Lockhart, Deborah F. Dynamic buckling of a damped imperfect column on a nonlinear foundation. ''Quart. Appl. Math.'' 36 (1978/79), no. 1, 49–55.
